shouldFix.title: The stated live-cell delimiter rule is false against the live DR-G16 evidence cell, and applying it in either direction produces the five-way split the same object forbids
shouldFix.charge: liveCellMemberSplit.delimiter reads 'comma, then coordinating and'. The live DR-G16 evidence cell is 'selected-lane explanation, per-lane signed closure evidence, skipped-lane proof, shared-core and cross-component protocol/semantic/lock/offline/bundle results'. Its members are delimited by comma alone - commas at offsets 25, 59 and 79 - and the single ' and ' in the cell, at offset 92, sits INSIDE the fourth member between 'shared-core' and 'cross-component'. The file itself says so at liveCellMemberSplit.slashJoiner: 'shared-core and cross-component is a compound modifier of that results phrase, not two live-cell members.' So the delimiter field contradicts its own sibling field. Both readings of the field fail against live bytes. As a JOIN rule: joining membersInOrder with commas and a coordinating 'and' before the last yields '...skipped-lane proof and shared-core and cross-component protocol/semantic/lock/offline/bundle results', which is not the live cell (string equality False); the plain-comma join is (equality True). As a SPLIT rule: applying 'comma, then coordinating and' to the live cell - split on the final coordinating ' and ', then on commas - yields FIVE members: ['selected-lane explanation', 'per-lane signed closure evidence', 'skipped-lane proof', 'shared-core', 'cross-component protocol/semantic/lock/offline/bundle results']. That is precisely the corruption this same object forbids at notInventedExtras ('shared-core as a fifth live-cell member', 'cross-component as a sixth live-cell member'), that failsIf forbids ('shared-core and cross-component protocol/semantic/lock/offline/bundle results is split into six live-cell members'), and that this cycle's dispatch attacks ('the fourth live-cell member is split into six members'). The field is not decorative and it is not boilerplate: across this harness family it is authored per cell and stated precisely, and the neighbouring files prove the vocabulary exists to state G16's case correctly - harness.DR-G10 'coordinating and; no comma', harness.DR-G18 'comma; no coordinating and before the last member', harness.DR-G19 'comma, then coordinating and, then semicolon', harness.DR-G20 'semicolon; no comma; one coordinating and inside the first semicolon field'. The four files that do carry 'comma, then coordinating and' - G07, G08, G14, G22 - have cells that genuinely take a coordinating 'and' before the last member (G07: 'descriptor/identity and race results'; G14: 'typed remediation and approved-exception diagnostics'). G16's cell does not. This reads as a copy-forward of the G07/G14 variant onto a cell with different punctuation, and G20's delimiter shows the house form for exactly this case: an 'and' that is internal to a member is named as internal rather than as a delimiter.
shouldFix.whyNotABlocker: The derived RESULT is correct and independently corroborated. membersInOrder and the four retainedEvidence memberVerbatim values are right, their plain-comma rejoin reproduces the live cell character-for-character, and monorepo-ci-contract.v16 - dual-ACCEPTed at D-124 - independently decomposed the same live cell into G16-OBL-4..G16-OBL-7 with OBL-7 carrying the fourth member whole. Nothing in this artifact is actually mis-split, and it binds NOTHING at CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED. The defect is the stated rule, not the output it accompanies. But a false derivation rule sitting beside a correct result is exactly the kind of text a later fixture-authoring cycle re-derives from, and re-deriving from it yields the forbidden split.
shouldFix.whatWouldLandIt: Replace the value with the punctuation this cell actually has, in the form the family already uses - the G18 statement plus the G20-style internal-and note. For example: 'comma; no coordinating and before the last member; the single and is internal to the fourth member (shared-core and cross-component)'. No other field needs to change: slashJoiner, membersInOrder, notInventedExtras and notCollapsed are already correct, and the four retainedEvidence members already carry the right strings.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: One SHOULD-FIX, no blockers. liveCellMemberSplit.delimiter states 'comma, then coordinating and', but the live DR-G16 evidence cell delimits its four members by comma alone - the one ' and ' in the cell is internal to the fourth member, between 'shared-core' and 'cross-component', exactly as the file's own slashJoiner says. Applied as a join rule it does not reproduce the live cell; applied as a split rule it yields five members, splitting 'shared-core' off as a fifth - the corruption this same object forbids at notInventedExtras and failsIf and that the dispatch attacks. The field is authored per cell across this harness family (G10 'coordinating and; no comma', G18 'comma; no coordinating and before the last member', G20 'semicolon; no comma; one coordinating and inside the first semicolon field'), and G07/G14, which legitimately carry this variant, have cells that do take a coordinating and before the last member. This is a copy-forward onto a cell with different punctuation. It is not a blocker: the derived result is correct, reproduces the live cell character-for-character under plain commas, and matches the independent G16-OBL-4..7 decomposition in the dual-ACCEPTed v16. Everything else verified clean - 8/8 cited digests, all seven verbatim carries exact, the three harness-cell corpus classes derived correctly after the named-identifier sentence, all six file-02 limb quotes exact, DR-121's 'authority' correctly kept out of G16's 'semantic', EE-7e correctly a ride and not a fifth member, zero v16 identifiers adopted, and no QUALIFIED, SATISFIED, G13-into-required-now, Rust-as-core, D9 code or 7.1 recipe anywhere.
